description: The oracle: run the markdown `/pan:exec-phase 1 --skip-tests` on the same two-plan seed and assert the same outcomes as the native run.
why: Oracle diffing (stability doctrine). A native workflow is only worth shipping if its chain completes at least as often as the prose path it ports. Same seed, same assertions, different orchestration — the comparison is the finding, not either run alone. Run --repeat 5 alongside native-exec-waves-chain.

steps.why: Identical outcome assertions to the native run, minus the verification file, which the markdown path also writes (exec-phase's verify_phase_goal; the seed leaves `workflow.verifier` on) and this scenario does not yet assert. The session persists so the last step can read what each executor opened.
Working code, not files that look right.

Memory optimisation O2: exec-phase writes the phase's roadmap slice, and the seed's plans still name `@.planning/roadmap.md` in their <context>, as plans written before slices do. An executor must read the slice in its place. Counted from the executors' own transcripts.
